# education materials library submission

## Share your work with other educators!

Interested in sharing the resources you’ve developed using open data from the Allen Institute? We would love to showcase your work and share it with other educators via the Allen Institute Materials Library.

In order to submit your work to be considered for sharing, please complete the steps listed below.

#### Questions?

Check out our FAQ or reach out to us at education@alleninstitute.org.

#### Step 1: Templates

Use the following templates to format the final drafts of your resource(s):

powerpoint template

#### Step 2: Accessibility

Please check to make sure your materials meet the following accessibility requirements and are compatible with screen readers:

- Alt-Text: Ensure that all images, figures, and/or objects have alt-text.
- Headings: Ensure all documents use headings to aid screen reader navigation.

For more information on formatting and accessibility, see the UC Irvine Teaching Accessibility Guide.

#### Step 3: Framework & Standards Alignment

Please align your resource(s) to the core concepts and core competencies from Vision & Change (2011). See here for a non-exhaustive list of other frameworks you may consider aligning your resource(s) with.

Made with BioRender.com

#### Step 4: Submission Terms & Conditions

Resources within our materials library are licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Please see here for our Submission Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy.

We also ask that you include the following excerpt at the end of your resource:

“This resource was created with support from the Allen Institute. This work is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial–ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). To view a copy of this license, visit https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/.“

#### Step 5: Submission Form

Submit the final drafts of your materials by completing and submitting the form below! Want to write out your responses to the submission form before you hit submit? Feel free to use this word template.

finalRoute.subject: Student mentorship inquiry: appropriate contact for Dr Akira Fushiki
finalRoute.body:
Dear Allen Institute Education team,

I'm Ethan Ramli, a grade 11 student in Jakarta. I'm hoping to ask Dr Akira Fushiki a small scientific question connected to his research and see whether he would consider occasional mentorship. I couldn't find a current direct address, and your general contact form would not allow me to submit. Could you please forward the note below, or advise me on an appropriate professional contact? I understand if this is outside your team's remit.

Thank you,
Ethan Ramli

----- For Dr Akira Fushiki -----

Dear Dr Fushiki,

I'm Ethan Ramli, a 16-year-old Singaporean grade 11 student in Jakarta. Chess and the public adult fly connectome led me to ask whether a model constrained by that wiring could learn useful decisions through experience and feedback.

Your earlier fly work on recurrent learning circuits, and your current work on different dopamine populations at the Allen Institute, connect to a problem I'm stuck on. I don't want to turn every kind of feedback into the same signal just because that is easier to code. What evidence would justify keeping different dopamine populations as separate teaching channels in a simplified model?

In six simple association tests, the model preferred the rewarded option more after training. But when I changed which option earned the reward, it chose the new option in only three tests, so it failed the full test. I haven't established whether the mechanism is biologically sound. The chess part currently records feedback without learning from it.

I define the research question and training rubric, AI makes most of the code, and I am still learning the underlying methods. I have no research adviser. I'd like to develop this into a sound study that I could eventually submit to eLife.

Would you be open to occasional mentorship, starting with whether this part of the approach makes sense? I'd appreciate a candid assessment and can send a one-page methods summary first.

Thank you for your time,
Ethan Ramli
High-school student | Jakarta, Indonesia
